title: NB Harness Module Manifest
description: The contract every NB module ships as nb-module.json. Without it a module is just a prompt bundle; this schema makes module boundaries machine-readable so 'run only security' works, and so the strength auto-judge (blueprint 3.9) can read each module's risk from permissions/side_effects.

required_in.description: Required inputs (e.g. security <- code_path, design <- intent). Empty array = self-contained entry module.

optional_in.description: Optional inputs that deepen the result (synergy). e.g. security + design_docs -> structural (layer-3) checks.

artifact.description: Output path; may use the {WORKSPACE} variable.

outputs.description: Named output artifacts the next module can consume.

verify_cmd.description: Command that verifies this module's own result. May use {VERIFY_CMD}. null when not applicable (e.g. design produces docs).

action.description: What the harness does when the condition hits.

failure_states.description: Failure conditions plus what happens (STOP / degrade / retry).

success.description: Signal emitted on success; the next module reads this.

permissions.description: Capabilities this module requests. Visible to AI and human so risk is explicit.

side_effects.description: Concrete side effects (writes files? network calls? external state change?).

install_deps.description: Dependencies to install. If non-empty, the install-safety flow (blueprint 11.3) applies: show plan -> user approves -> pin version -> local.

requires_approval.description: Whether execution needs explicit user approval before running (risky action = true). The strength auto-judge never auto-runs a true here (blueprint 3.9 / 11.2).

safety_gates.description: Which safety gates apply (blueprint 3.5 self-check, 11.2 security execution gate).

modes.description: Optional execution modes at different strength (security: analysis / red_team_sim / sandbox_attack).
